title: The Street Where Tourists Risk Their Lives for a Photo
paragraphs: In the center of Hanoi, the capital of Vietnam, there is a very narrow street with a railway track running down the middle. Real passenger trains pass through it, very close to the buildings on both sides. This place, known as "Train Street," has become one of the city's most popular tourist attractions, but it is also one of the most dangerous.

The railway was built by the French in the early 1900s, when Vietnam was a French colony. For many years, the area was poor and run-down. However, thanks to social media, it has now become famous. Today, the street is lined with cafes where tourists sit next to the tracks, drinking coffee and waiting to take photos and videos of the train as it passes. The train moves at about 10 kilometers per hour.
For many visitors, being so close to a moving train is exciting. "I feel adrenaline because (the train) was so close," a tourist from Slovakia said.

However, the street has had many dangerous moments. Authorities closed it in 2019 after several near accidents, and in 2022, they ordered the cafes to close. But tourists kept coming back. In March 2025, police removed hundreds of tourists from the street. Then, in October 2025, a video went viral that showed a train hitting tables placed too close to the tracks, knocking them over as tourists jumped up in panic.

Some people think the street should be closed permanently for safety reasons. But cafe owners say that tourism has made the area cleaner and safer. Some even suggest building a fence instead of closing the street.
Hanoi is not the only place like this. There are similar "train streets" in Thailand and Taiwan, and they also attract thousands of tourists.
